segment: Motorcycle-side fleet buyers in Southern California: P2P rental platforms (Riders Share, Twisted Road), motorcycle/scooter rental and tour companies, rider training (CMSP, H-D Riding Academy), film/TV picture-vehicle houses, security/BID patrol contractors, municipal e-moto (LAPD/LASD/Metro/rangers)
summary: Research completed 2026-09-09 within a 14-call budget; several items rest on 1-2 sources and are tagged accordingly. Honest verdict: on the motorcycle side there is no identifiable Southern California buyer who purchases 10-50 unbranded electric motorcycles in one order. Rental (EagleRider) chose electric brands through OEM partnerships (Zero 2021, LiveWire) rather than fleet tenders; P2P platforms (Riders Share, Twisted Road) are not buyers at all but are a near-zero-cost way for HMP to put its own 5-10 demo FLASH/MK.II units to work at roughly $60-120/day (LiveWire listings in LA fetch ~$199/day, Riders Share hosts keep 60-75% of booking profit). CMSP training sites run 125-250cc gas bikes supplied by the site operator under a CHP/Total Control Training curriculum; a 75 mph FLASH is unsuitable for beginners and a clutch-less MK.II cannot teach the clutch/gear skills the MTC exists to test, so training is a zero-unit segment unless CHP/TCT approves an electric curriculum. Film picture-vehicle houses (Malibu Autobahn, Cinema Vehicles, Angel City Motorcycles, Galpin Rentals, Venice Vintage) own their inventory and buy opportunistically 1-3 units at a time when a script calls for a look; none advertises electric motorcycles today, so a placement is plausible but small. Police/BID patrol wants pedal-assist MTBs or a police-packaged Zero (LAPD has run Zero MMX/off-road units since 2014 and added all-electric units in 2020); HMP has no police package, no cooperative-contract listing and no FMVSS-tested lighting/siren kit, so municipal is zero units in 12 months. Realistic 12-month motorcycle-side volume: 0-20 units, base case ~6, most of them HMP's own demo bikes placed on P2P platforms plus 1-3 opportunistic film/rental sales. The lucrative route on this side is marketing (test rides that convert to retail sales), not fleet revenue.

CMSP is administered by the CHP through primary contractor Total Control Training Inc.; over 1.5 million riders trained since July 1987 as of June 2025; the Motorcyclist Training Course (MTC) is 15 hours (5 classroom, 10 riding) and earns the DMV skills-test waiver
CMSP training sites provide the motorcycle, helmet and gloves in the course fee; training bikes are 125-250cc (site FAQs at Golden State Moto, 2 Wheel Safety, Twysted Throttle, AMO SoCal)
Training fleets are owned or leased by each site operator (the CMSP sponsor), not by CHP; replacement cycles are not published
Total Control's 'eRider' is the online-classroom version of the MTC (4-6 hours), not an electric-motorcycle course; no CMSP site was found using electric training motorcycles

Harley-Davidson Riding Academy in SoCal runs at Harley-Davidson of Glendale (3717 San Fernando Rd, Glendale 91204; AMO SoCal uses the dealership classroom) and Huntington Beach Harley-Davidson (15080 Goldenwest Circle, Westminster 92683); Los Angeles Harley-Davidson closed permanently 2024-10-31
Harley-Davidson Riding Academy dealers train on H-D-supplied bikes under the H-D/MSF curriculum and will not add a non-H-D electric motorcycle

Malibu Autobahn (picture cars, 4,000+ movie/production vehicles) rents its own motorcycle inventory to film/TV/commercials: sport bikes, dirt bikes, cruisers, vintage to a 2024 BMW F900R; no electric motorcycle or scooter is listed; contact 310-776-5163 / contactus@malibuautobahn.com

Cinema Vehicles (family-run since 1975) supplies 1,600+ movie vehicles including motorcycles; Angel City Motorcycles says it is the only LA business exclusively renting motorcycles for film/photo/events with transport, on-set wrangling and stunt doubles; Galpin Rentals supplies picture vehicles and new vehicles 'from all manufacturers'; Venice Vintage Motorcycle Club and Glory Motorworks (since 1999) supply motorcycles and props

LAPD's Off-Road Unit has operated six Zero electric off-road motorcycles (MMX) since 2014 for parks and mountain areas; LAPD issued a Jan 2020 news release on additional all-electric motorcycles (NR20014ti)

No 2023-2026 LAPD, LASD, LA Metro Transit Security or park-ranger electric motorcycle purchase, and no Sourcewell/cooperative-contract award for Zero or LiveWire, surfaced in one targeted search; treat municipal e-moto demand as unverified rather than absent

Police buyers require a police package (emergency lighting, siren, radio/computer mount, crash bars, service training) and a cooperative or competitively bid contract vehicle; HMP has none of these today

how_to_reach: List 5-10 HMP-owned FLASH/MK.II demo units on Riders Share (Standard 75% plan) and Twisted Road from the LA site; price $60-120/day against LiveWire at $199 and 300cc gas bikes at $31-60; use bookings as paid test rides and offer a rental credit toward purchase (copying Zero's $300 EagleRider credit).

Pitch EagleRider corporate partnerships (eaglerider.com/franchise contact path; HQ is 3 miles from LAX at 11860 S La Cienega) with a consignment/demo proposal rather than a sale: HMP supplies 3-5 FLASH Plus units, EagleRider keeps rental revenue, HMP gets the try-before-you-buy funnel.

Send a one-page spec sheet with day-rate and stunt-pair availability to LA picture-vehicle houses (Malibu Autobahn 310-776-5163 / contactus@malibuautobahn.com; Cinema Vehicles; Angel City Motorcycles; Galpin Rentals; Venice Vintage) and list HMP itself on ProductionHub and LA 411 as a picture-vehicle supplier; expect 1-3 unit buys or per-day rentals, not fleets.

Do not pursue CMSP or Riding Academy fleets in the next 12 months; if desired later, approach Total Control Training HQ (not individual sites) with a low-power-mode MK.II and crash-bar kit for a pilot, and expect a multi-year approval path.
Do not pursue LAPD/LASD/Metro until HMP has a police package and a cooperative-contract listing; benchmark against Zero DSRP pricing first.
Verify Riders Share LA listing counts and rates by opening the site in a normal browser (pages are JS/cookie-walled to the proxy).
constraints: FLASH/MK.II are DOT motorcycles: renters need an M1 license and the renter's license must be checked (CVC 14608/14609); tourist scooter fleets already accept this for 150cc Vespas but it filters out most walk-up tourists.
Commercial rental insurance for motorcycles is scarce; P2P platforms supply it (Lloyd's via Riders Share; $100k/$25k via Twisted Road), which is why self-listing beats building a rental counter.
California DMV dealer license is required to sell FLASH/MK.II retail in CA; film houses and rental shops will buy only titled, registered, plated units.
CMSP training bikes must fit the CHP/Total Control curriculum (125-250cc class, manual clutch for MTC skills, crash protection); no electric approval exists.
Police fleets need a police package (lighting, siren, radio mount), FMVSS-compliant lighting, dealer service SLA and a bid or cooperative contract; none exists for HMP.
Picture-vehicle houses buy 1-3 units for a look, not 10-50; they also expect low-cost service and parts on call.
Zero's 'Try Before You Buy' and EagleRider co-marketing set the template; HMP must fund demo units and credits itself.
what_hmp_must_have: 5-10 registered, insured, plated demo FLASH/MK.II units at the LA site with GPS trackers and a keyed/immobilizer setup acceptable to P2P platforms
Production-ready spec sheet: dimensions, weight, top speed, charge time, sound (silent), stunt-pair availability, on-set charging plan
Loaner/consignment agreement template for EagleRider or a rental shop (HMP retains title, operator keeps revenue share)
For any future training or police pilot: low-power/limited-speed mode, crash bars, and a service SLA

realistic_12mo_units.rationale: No SoCal buyer was found that purchases 10-50 unbranded electric motorcycles in one order. Base case is HMP's own 5-8 demo units placed on Riders Share/Twisted Road (revenue, not unit sales) plus 1-3 opportunistic sales to picture-vehicle houses. High case adds a 3-5 unit consignment at EagleRider LA and a 2-5 unit tourist-rental trial (Santa Barbara/Palm Springs). Training and municipal segments are zero in 12 months because of curriculum/police-package barriers.

red_flags: Two of the six requested sub-segments (CMSP training, municipal e-moto) are structurally closed to HMP products as they exist today; investing sales time there would be wasted.
EagleRider's electric rentals came through OEM partnerships with Zero and LiveWire; a small importer without a service network is unlikely to get the same deal without funding the units.
Riders Share LA listing pages and EagleRider franchise page were not readable through the proxy; LA electric-listing counts and EagleRider fleet-ownership model remain unverified.
P2P rental exposes demo units to crash/theft; Riders Share coverage is 'up to $30,000' per rental, and hosts on the Standard plan bear mechanical repairs.
Film placements are episodic; a picture-car house may rent rather than buy, and needs stunt pairs (2 identical units) for action scenes.
Most evidence on Twisted Road/LiveWire and LAPD Zero purchases is 2014-2021; current activity is inferred from listings that still exist rather than fresh announcements.
The previous partial file on security/BIDs found patrol buyers prefer pedal-assist MTBs; this run added nothing that changes that verdict (no BID moped/motorcycle patrol procurement surfaced).
